svg.title: SCALING READS: sketchnote
svg.text: Most systems read far more than they write. Make the common read cheap, and the database only sees
The same items are read over and over
A read path misses its latency target, or the
calculated read QPS exceeds what one
One database serves every read. At ~10k+
Cache-aside: check Redis; on a miss, read the

Read replicas spread the remaining reads
CDN serves static and shared responses from
the edge, so origin never sees them.
Is the response the same for many users?
Is it per-user but read often? Cache-aside in
Still too much load on the primary? Add read
Is one key extremely hot? Replicate the key
or add a short-lived local cache.
Which reads must never be stale? Send those
popularity is skewed, so a cache-aside Redis

replicas; only checkout reads the primary."
Sharding the database before trying a cache and replicas.
Caching data that must be exact (stock at checkout, balances).
Forgetting cache stampedes on hot keys.
Used in: URL shortener (Bitly), Rate limiter, Business discovery
(Yelp), News feed (Facebook), News aggregator (Google News), Local
delivery (Gopuff), Dating app (Tinder), Distributed cache, Post
